\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
\title{A one-bit condition can leave the semisimple-dual family}
\date{28 October 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
This obstruction concerns closure of the inherited certificate, not
hardness of the resulting count or rejection by every possible frontend.
Work over $\mathbb F_2$ in $M_8(\mathbb F_2)$ and put
\[
 \mathcal D=\{\operatorname{diag}(A,A,B,B):A,B\in M_2(\mathbb F_2)\},
 \qquad W=\mathcal D^\perp
\]
under $\langle D,Y\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(DY)$.
The right entry $Y_{31}$ is an independent free coordinate of $W$.
Pinning that one input bit to zero changes the reverse dual to
\[
 \mathcal D'=\mathcal D+\langle E_{13}\rangle,
\]
since $\operatorname{tr}(E_{13}Y)=Y_{31}$ and $E_{13}\notin\mathcal D$.

Its actual left multiplier algebra is
\[
 \{T:T\mathcal D'\subseteq\mathcal D'\}
 =\{\operatorname{diag}(A,A,B,B): A_{21}=0\}
 \simeq \operatorname{UT}_2(\mathbb F_2)\oplus M_2(\mathbb F_2).
\]
Indeed $I\in\mathcal D'$, so any multiplier has form
$T=\operatorname{diag}(A,A,B,B)+bE_{13}$. Multiplication by an old
diagonal element with first block $C$ creates the term $bC_{12}E_{14}$,
forcing $b=0$. Then $TE_{13}=A_{11}E_{13}+A_{21}E_{23}$, forcing
$A_{21}=0$. Conversely these conditions suffice on every basis element.

The first factor has the nonzero square-zero radical generated by
$\operatorname{diag}(E_{12},E_{12},0,0)$. Therefore the retained full
simple-factor/sandwich test cannot certify this multiplier algebra as
semisimple. The regular two-factor representation is not closed under
even this legal one-bit restriction. A general prefix sampler cannot
be inferred from the count theorem without an additional representation
or direct fiber-sampling argument. Signed histogram coefficients likewise
do not provide nonnegative branching probabilities.
\end{document}

## E. Failures, comparisons and evidence levels

Pinning a legal right bit in the repeated-block M8 example adds E13 to the
dual and changes its multiplier to UT2(F2) plus M2(F2), with a nonzero
square-zero radical. Thus the inherited semisimple certificate is not closed
under these conditions. This refutes that self-reduction argument, not all
sampling methods or conditioned-count hardness. The separate old diamond
transfer counts ordered crossing pairs with a common target carrier; it
does not cover arbitrary crossings or replace the distinct-carrier theorem.

The final 72-input E6 fixture, its all-output section and its generic sampler
share one acquired certificate in the source integration record. At c=8,
the generic 256-character fallback is already feasible; this is an admission
and correctness example, not E6 speed evidence. The high-c formula run is
explicitly formula-only, not a raw-circuit acquisition. The retained audit
target-shift error was in the harness; production correctly declined it.

The ordinary comparison uses a DIFFERENT 72-input, 24676-gate crossing
fixture with full-equivalence unique-extension Tseitin encoding. Source
records show d4 and SharpSAT-TD count timeouts at 120 seconds, and a separate
d4 compilation timeout with an empty invalid artifact. Sampling was not
reached; there is no measured sampling ratio, ordinary SAT witness timing,
broad portfolio result or independent large-count validation from those
timeouts. New crossing pipeline time 23.1144 seconds and E6 pipeline time
19.6630 seconds must not be compared as matched fixtures. The specified
source executions, compiler pins, controls and limits remain visible.

No theorem here solves unrestricted Boolean counting. No novelty, physical
measurement, working device, practical advantage or mission achievement is
inferred. Internally verified mathematics is accepted without adding an
external-review prerequisite; genuine recognition, cost, conditioning and
implementation qualifications remain.
